title: proto_find_undecoded_data's marking loop is bounded by the field's extent and not by the bitmap's length, so a field reaching past the frame writes off the end
object: decoded, a packet-scope chunk of length/8 + 1 bytes
lifetime_ender: NONE -- the object is alive throughout. This is a SPATIAL row.
shape: `for (i = fi->start; i < fi->start + fi->length; i++) { decoded[i/8] |= 1 << (i%8); }` consults the FIELD extent only, so a field whose start plus length reaches past the frame drives the byte index past the bitmap
allocator_layer: wmem, a chunk the BLOCK or BLOCK_FAST allocator carved from a block g_malloc handed out. An inner allocator carved the crossed region, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row IS NESTED.
nested_why: an inner allocator (wmem) carved the crossed region out of a larger block it had itself obtained from g_malloc, so under this inventory's axis -- WHO ALLOCATED THE OBJECT -- this row IS NESTED.
fidelity: real allocator, model consumer. the frame is 64 bytes, so the bitmap is 9. The field claims start 56 and length 32, reaching index 87 and byte 10 -- past the bitmap and inside the block, both asserted.
live_proof: read from the PINNED source: v4.6.8:epan/proto.c contains the fix's `decoded_data_t` struct 4 times and the pre-fix bare `gchar* decoded = (gchar*)wmem_alloc0` 0 times. Two-sided. A fix-reversal.
distinguishing: the index here comes from the protocol tree's OWN field extents -- output of a sibling subsystem -- rather than from attacker-supplied lengths as in rows 14 and 18. The fix accordingly does not clamp the field; it threads the bitmap's length through a struct and bounds the write. That is why this is not a duplicate of the clamp rows.

cheribsd-revocation.target: stock CheriBSD purecap with libc revocation on
cheribsd-revocation.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-10, results/2026-10-10-cheribsd-libc/: **NOT CAUGHT** on stock wmem with the system allocator as CheriBSD's libc (WM_LIBC_SYSTEM, WM_CHUNKS=OFF), revocation on: the crossing stayed inside one g_malloc'd block and completed; fixed arm VERDICT FIXED. In the same boot control 90 (a jumbo g_free'd by the reset) was HELD by the quarantine and the revocation control faulted at its labelled load. The 2026-10-07 reading of this arm ran the hosted bump arena with the chunk port compiled in, where nothing reached free().

native-detect.oracle: MEASURED 2026-10-09, results/2026-10-09-native-asan/: **NO ASan REPORT** on the buggy arm, which printed VERDICT DEFECT-REPRODUCED, so the defective access ran and ASan did not see it. The fixed arm exits 0 with VERDICT FIXED and no report. Built with the port's own allocator library under the same sanitizer (cc (Ubuntu 13.3.0-6ubuntu2~24.04.1) 13.3.0; -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -g -O0; wmem and the port built with the same flags). Positive controls in the same run: `asan-control past 402653184` -> heap-buffer-overflow; `asan-control uaf 402653184` -> heap-use-after-free -- so ASan reports on a heap block the size of this corpus's arena, and the silence is the arena: one malloc'd block, carved and recycled without free(). Predicted before the run (b64cd18b85d0); the arm was previously 'not written'.
native-detect.measured: 2026-10-10, results/2026-10-10-native-asan-libc/run-asan.txt: SILENT, the defect reproduced; wmem built with WM_LIBC_SYSTEM=ON (g_malloc/g_free are the host's malloc/free); wmem's own control 90 reported heap-use-after-free at wm_probe in the same run. The earlier reading (2026-10-09) ran the hosted bump arena, which could read nothing else.
